title: The Spire of the Glass Steppe
premise: Paloma Hartwell, last apprentice of the nearly extinct Wayfarers' Guild, is bound by oath to guide a dying stranger's map to the Glass Steppe — a mirror-flat plain hiding the court of the Mountain Below. The map's true cargo is the soul of Ivo Serrano, sold by his own brother to buy the court's favor, and Paloma discovers the stranger was Ivo himself, clinging to life long enough to hire her. Joined by a disgraced court musician and a moon-touched child who can hear souls singing, she must steal Ivo's soul back before the thirteenth turn of the moon seals it into the mountain forever. In the end Paloma trades her guild oath — the last living bond to her dead mentors — for Ivo's freedom, and finds that family is not inherited but chosen.
about_author: Wendell Vane spent a decade cataloguing folk songs in remote mountain villages before turning to fiction, and his prose still carries the cadence of ballads. He lives at the edge of a national forest with two opinionated goats and writes only by lamplight.

chapters.title: The Last Oath of Thornfell
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Wayfarers' Guild hall stands empty except for Paloma and her dying master, who reminds her the guild dies when its last oath does. A bloodied stranger stumbles in during a storm and presses a folded map into her hands, whispering 'thirteen turns' before collapsing. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by sudden, unwanted responsibility.

chapters.title: A Map Drawn in Dying Ink
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The stranger, Ivo Serrano, survives barely; the map shifts and rewrites itself each night, its ink made from something alive. He confesses fragments: he sold his own soul to the court beneath the mountain to save his brother, then changed his mind. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion hardening into resolve as Paloma accepts the contract.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road South
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with interludes from Ivo's fevered memories. She leads them through hidden passes only she knows, evading toll-keepers who serve the mountain court. Ivo's condition worsens the closer they get — his body forgetting how to be alive. Emotional beat: growing tenderness between guide and client, shadowed by guilt over her guild's failures.

chapters.title: The Musician Who Fell
chapters.summary: Sera Voss's POV. They find Sera, once the mountain court's favored musician, exiled for playing a lament for a stolen soul. She recognizes the map instantly and warns them: the court does not sell back what it buys. She joins them anyway. Emotional beat: found family begins forming around shared exile and shame.

chapters.title: The Child Who Hears Singing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In a steppe-edge village they meet Pip, an orphan who hears souls as music and says Ivo's song is 'almost finished.' Toll-keepers raid the village hunting the map; the group escapes with Pip clinging to Paloma's back. Emotional beat: Paloma realizes she has stopped traveling alone without noticing when it happened.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns of the Moon
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Crossing the Glass Steppe, which reflects not faces but regrets, Ivo confronts the memory of his brother's betrayal and his own bargain. The moon wanes toward its final turn; his heartbeat grows fainter each night. Emotional beat: acceptance of death transformed into fierce desire to live honestly, however briefly remains.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Guided by Pip's hearing, they descend through a fault into the glass-walled court, where souls hang like lanterns. Paloma bargains with the Pale Steward using smuggler's guile, but learns the price of return: a binding of equal weight. Emotional beat: dread and wonder entwined as duty and love begin pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: What the Steward Asks
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The Steward names its price: the guild oath that anchors Paloma's identity, or Ivo walks out soulless. Sera plays the lament that once got her exiled, buying time while Paloma decides. Ivo begs her to refuse. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal — the choice that defines the book.

chapters.title: The Stealing of a Soul
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. While the court sleeps to Sera's music, Paloma uses every smuggler's trick she knows to lift Ivo's lantern-soul, Pip singing to mask its light. The Steward wakes; the escape becomes a running battle up the fault as the thirteenth moon rises. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into triumph through trust in her chosen family.

chapters.title: Where the Wayfarers End
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On the steppe at moonrise, Paloma surrenders her oath to the Steward's messenger, unbinding herself — and the guild ends so that Ivo may live. They bury the map, which finally goes still. Epilogue beat: spring on the steppe, four travelers building a new waystation together, no oaths needed. Emotional beat: grief braided with belonging; an ending that is also a beginning.
